title: Reverse through shared memory
starter:
%x = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=1
# Reverse each block of 8 elements, through shared memory.
%sh = alloc 8 dtype=f32
%b = range 4 axis=global
%m = mul %b 8
# phase 1: thread t copies x[8b + t] into sh[t]
%t = range 8 axis=local
%i = add %m %t
%xv = shrink %x %i shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%sv = shrink %sh %t shape=[]
%s1 = store %sv %xe
%e1 = end %s1 %t
%sh1 = after %sh %e1
# phase 2: thread u writes o[8b + u]: it should read the element at the mirror position, sh[7 - u]
%u = range 8 axis=local
%ru = add %u 0
%rv = shrink %sh1 %ru shape=[]
%re = load %rv
%j = add %m %u
%ov = shrink %o %j shape=[]
%s2 = store %ov %re
%e2 = end %s2 %u
%eb = end %e1 %e2 %b
%o1 = after %o %eb
hints: Phase 2 reads sh[u], which copies the block unchanged. The mirror of position u in 8 is 7 - u.
Reading another thread's slot is fine here: it was written in phase 1, and the barrier between phases makes sure every thread finished it.

answer.code:
%x = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%o = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=1
# Reverse each block of 8 elements, through shared memory.
%sh = alloc 8 dtype=f32
%b = range 4 axis=global
%m = mul %b 8
# phase 1: thread t copies x[8b + t] into sh[t]
%t = range 8 axis=local
%i = add %m %t
%xv = shrink %x %i shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%sv = shrink %sh %t shape=[]
%s1 = store %sv %xe
%e1 = end %s1 %t
%sh1 = after %sh %e1
# phase 2: thread u writes o[8b + u]
%u = range 8 axis=local
%nu = mul %u -1
%ru = add %nu 7
%rv = shrink %sh1 %ru shape=[]
%re = load %rv
%j = add %m %u
%ov = shrink %o %j shape=[]
%s2 = store %ov %re
%e2 = end %s2 %u
%eb = end %e1 %e2 %b
%o1 = after %o %eb
answer.explain: The two loops are two phases of one block. In phase 2, thread u reads the slot thread 7 - u wrote in phase 1. That's only safe because a phase ends with every thread waiting at a barrier, which the CUDA renderer writes as __syncthreads(). Reading another thread's slot in the same phase would be a race, and the rule rejects it.
